Later
You will find what comes next in the Guide, with the book at the top of the home screen.
The demo is not installed
This tutorial begins in the demo. Reinstall it, or skip its steps there.
Skip those steps
These tutorials use the demo: %1$s. Without it, their steps in the demo are skipped. You can reinstall it at any time from Settings › Demo.
First steps
After a look around the demo, you create a first zone and a first tool, with no AI needed.

You now have a zone and a tool to note entries in. To choose the next ones, look through the “The tools” part of the Guide. To start from a tool of the demo, touch the + of a section in your zone, then “A tool” under Copy: the copy stays when the demo is removed. With an AI, you can also describe the tool you want. What remains is to connect an AI.
Open the zone Running

The demo follows Camille, who is training for a half marathon. Camille sorts life into zones, one per area, and running is one of them. In each zone, Camille notes what matters with tools, sorted here into three groups: Training, Body and Analysis.
Add a run in Runs

Runs is a Tracking tool. Each run is noted in it with its date and its kilometres. A figure noted this way is called an entry.\n\nTouch + to add one. The buttons under the title are shortcuts: one touch, and the entry is noted.
Open Km per week
The run just added already shows in this chart, and counts towards the goal “Training week”. An entry is noted once and shows up wherever it counts: chart, goal, variable.
Create your own zone, under “Ungrouped”

Go back to the home screen, scroll down to the “Ungrouped” section at the very bottom, and touch its +. Give the zone a name, an icon and a short description.\n\nNot in the Demo group, which belongs to Camille. Groups of your own come later, with the gear of the home screen.
Add a tool to it

In the zone, touch the + of a section, then choose a tool type. List is the simplest. It holds things to do, shopping or tasks, ticked once done.\n\nThe configuration screen shows many settings, but only the name is required, the others already have a value. Give the list a name, then confirm at the bottom of the screen.
Add a first entry to it
Open the list, type something to do and add it, then tick it once done.\n\nTo change the list later, touch and hold its title to open its configuration.
Connect an AI
The AI can do the same things as you in the app: read the tools, fill them in and set them up. For that, the app calls an AI provider: a service with your access key, or a server of your own.
The AI is connected. What remains is to build tools with it.
Open the AI providers
AI providers are set up in the Settings: Claude, OpenAI, DeepSeek, or another server, such as Ollama, LM Studio or OpenRouter.
Add a provider

For a service, first create an API key on its website. In the app, touch Add a provider, choose what it is, paste the key if it asks for one, choose a model and save.\n\nThe key stays on the phone, and the app sends it only to that provider. The first provider you add is the default: every new conversation takes it.
What it costs

With a service, each exchange is paid to it, with the key, and the conversation shows what each one cost. On a server of your own, nothing is paid: set its prices to 0 in its configuration, or its cost stays unknown.\n\nTo spend less, the provider\'s configuration has three settings: a smaller model, less reasoning, shorter answers with the token limit. In Settings › AI limits, you also set how many calls the AI may chain on its own before handing back.
Ask it for an overview
Touch the bubble to open the conversation, and ask the AI what it sees of the app. There is no need to attach anything. It already knows the zones and tools, and reads the entries it needs by itself.
Tell it about your tool with a pointer

A pointer is how you show the AI exactly what you mean.

Write a question, for example “What do you think of this list?”. Touch the crosshair under the message to add a pointer. In the “Select data” window, touch the zone, then the tool. Tick nothing, touch Confirm, then send the message.

Ticking Config or Entries would have attached that data to the message. The “Talk to the AI” chapter explains when that helps.
Configure a tool
Every tool has the same basic configuration: a name, an icon, a tile size in the zone, and fields added by hand. This chapter needs no AI.
You now know how to fit a tool to the way you use it, and how to take its entries out.
Open a tool\'s configuration
In a zone, press and hold a tool\'s title, for example the list made in First steps, to open its configuration. The General settings come first, the same for every tool, then those of its type.
Change its icon and its shape

Tap the icon to pick another one, and give it a colour. A Texture lays a motif on its tile and over the whole background of its screen. The Display mode sets the size of the tile in the zone, from Icon, the smallest, to Full, which shows everything. Save, then look at the zone.
Add a field of your own

An extra field lets you note more than the tool provides for, for example the shop of a purchase.\n\nOpen the configuration again. Under Extra fields, add a “Shop” field of the text type, then save. Then add an entry to the tool: the Shop field is in the form. Fill it in.
What concerns the AI

Two settings matter when the AI works on this tool.
- Data validation: the AI asks for your approval before changing the entries
- Always send to the AI: the entries go with every message, without the AI having to ask for them
An extra field can also be Read-only for the AI: the AI reads it, but only you fill it in. The tool's configuration is protected with its zone. The “Talk to the AI” chapter says more.
Export its entries

To read a tool\'s entries in a spreadsheet, touch “Export the entries…” in its configuration. Choose the period, the filters and the fields kept. Without a period, all the entries go.\n\nThe CSV file is written into the app\'s folder, and Share sends it wherever you like. The AI can also export a tool\'s entries, when you ask it to.
Build with the AI
Describe what you want to follow, and the AI creates the tools. Everything it does stays visible, and can be changed afterwards.
The AI built a tool and a variable with you. What remains is to have it work on its own, on a schedule.
What the AI can do
The AI creates and sets up tools, adds entries, writes variables and prepares routines, as you would. When a piece of information is missing, it asks with a field to fill in.
Ask the AI to create a tool

In the conversation, add a pointer to the zone and describe what you want to follow, for example “a tracker of the water I drink, in glasses”. Let the AI create the tool, or the step won\'t be marked done.
Look at the tool it made
Close the conversation and open the new tool. It is a tool like any other, changed through its configuration.
Have it create a variable
A variable is a figure worked out from entries, for example the number of glasses drunk today. Ask the AI for one: “a variable with today\'s glasses”. A goal or a chart can then use it.
Choose what it must ask before doing
In Settings › AI validation, you choose what the AI must show before acting. It then waits for your approval for each change, across the whole app, in a zone, in a tool or in a single conversation.
Routines
With a routine, a message for the AI is prepared once and used again as often as you like.
The routine is ready. The AI will handle it on its schedule, and you can run it or talk it over at any time. The rest is in Getting started, to read in any order.
What a routine is

A routine's message serves in two ways.

The AI can handle it on its own. It reads the tools, writes in them if the message asks for it, and the result is there to read later. With a schedule, it takes care of it by itself, every Sunday evening for example.

It can also be used to start a conversation with the AI, handy for a talk that comes back often, like “let's look back on my week”.

The AI can also create or change a routine for you. Ask it for example “set up a routine that sums up my meals every evening”.
Create a routine in a zone
A routine belongs to a zone, like a tool. In the zone, touch the + of a section, choose “Routine” and give it a name.
Write its message

Its tile sits in the section among the tools, in Extended by default: its state and its switch at the top, its four buttons under them. On the routine\'s tile, touch the pencil. Write what the AI should do, for example “sum up my week”. To have it run on its own, add a schedule, such as every Sunday at 6 pm. With Tell me when it ends, a notification tells you when it is done. Save.\n\nA long touch on its tile opens its settings: its name, its look, its provider. Shown smaller, its tile has no room for its buttons: touch it, its page has them all.
Run it once
To see what it does without waiting for its schedule, touch the play button on its tile, or on its page.
See what it did
Each run is kept in the routine\'s history. Touch one to see what the AI read, did and answered, and what it cost.
Or talk it over

On its tile, touch the bubble to start a conversation with the routine\'s message. It can go as it is or be changed first. This is the right choice to think things through with the AI rather than let it work alone.
Organize
When zones and tools pile up, you can sort them. Sorting works the same way at two levels: zones in groups on the home screen, and tools in groups within a zone.
Zones and tools are now sorted your way. Everything can be changed at any time, with the same gestures.
Two levels of sorting

On the home screen, zones are sorted into groups, each in its own section. In a zone, tools are sorted the same way. A zone or a tool without a group goes into the “Ungrouped” section.\n\nIn each section, tiles are placed on a grid, and their size depends on their display mode.
Create a group of zones

On the home screen, touch the gear at the top right to open the Home settings. Under Zone groups, add a Group, for example “Health”, then save. The home screen now shows one section per group, each with its own +.
Put a zone in that group

Press and hold a zone\'s tile to open its configuration. Choose the new group in Zone group, then save. The zone moves to that group\'s section.\n\nThe same configuration sets the Name of the zone, its Description, its Icon, the Icon colour and a Texture, a motif on its tile and over the whole ground of its page. Each of these two opens its own page: touch a choice to take it. A tool has the same three in its own configuration. With Protect this zone\'s content, the AI asks for your approval before changing what the zone holds. Its Identity, if you have one, is who the top of the zone opens a conversation with.
Move a tile

In a section, the layout mode is how tiles are placed.
- {layout-grid} Opens or closes the section's layout mode
Touch a tile to choose it, then move it with the arrows, one cell at a time. The other sections are greyed out meanwhile.
- {check} Confirms the move
- Cancel: puts the section back as it was
Choose a tile\'s size

In a zone\'s configuration, the Display mode sets the size of its tile on the home screen, from the smallest to the largest: Icon, Minimal, Line or Condensed. A larger tile also shows the zone\'s description.\n\nA tool has the same setting in its own configuration, with more sizes, up to Full.
Sort a zone\'s tools

Still in the zone\'s configuration, Tool groups lists its sections. Add a Tool group per subject, for example “Training” and “Analysis”.\n\nTo sort a tool, choose its Group in its configuration. The + of a section creates a tool right in that group, and the layout mode works here as on the home screen.
Connect tools
Tools can use each other\'s entries. This chapter shows the three ways to connect them: the reading, the variable and the Reference field.
The tools are now connected. The Goal and Chart chapters, in the Tools part, show how to use them.
Three ways to connect

- A reading draws a value from a tool's entries over a period: their sum, their average, the last one, or their count. A chart, a goal and a variable use it.
- A variable is a value with a name, fixed or worked out by a formula. It can be read anywhere: in a goal, a chart, another variable, or by the AI.
- A Reference field links an entry to another thing in the app, like a meal naming its foods.
Nothing is copied: each value is worked out again from the entries, at the moment it is read.
Create a fixed variable

A constant keeps a figure that comes from no entry, like a target of 2,000 kcal a day.\n\nIn a zone, touch the + of a section, then Variable. Choose the Kind Constant, give it a Name, for example target, which formulas write, a Label, for example Daily target, which its tile shows, and a Value. Save.
Create a worked-out variable

A formula works out its value from terms. In the same zone, create a new variable of Kind Formula.

Under Terms, touch “Add a term”. Give it a Name, for example total, and choose the Kind of term “Reading of entries”. Choose the tool, the Period, then What is read: a field, “The entries, counted” or “A formula in each entry”. Finally choose the Reduction, for example Sum. A term can also be a Fixed value or an Other variable.

In Formula, write the calculation with the names of the terms and of other variables, for example total - target. Save.
Read its value

A zone\'s variables show in their section among the tools, each on its tile, with its current value beside its label in Line, or under it in Condensed. When a value cannot be worked out, the reason shows in its place, for example an entry without an answer. Arrange moves their tiles like the tools\'.\n\nTouch a variable to change it. Its screen shows its value “Now”, its Label, its Description, its Icon, Icon colour, Texture and Display mode, its Type of the value, often Deduced from the formula, its Unit and its Number of decimals.
Link an entry to another

A Reference field lets an entry point to another thing in the app, for example a meal's foods, kept in a Structured data tool.

In a tool's configuration, add an extra field of type Reference. Under Target, Can point to says what the field accepts: The app, Zone, Tool, Entry or Variable. With Entry, “Entries of these tools only” narrows the choice to some tools.

In an entry, this field opens on the app, then you go down from zone to tool to the thing you want. The reference follows that thing, even when it is renamed.
Talk to the AI
This chapter covers the conversation with the AI: what you can attach, how it answers and asks for your approval, the settings of a conversation and what it costs.
You now know how to attach what is needed, answer the AI and set up a conversation. To have the AI do the same without you, read the Routines chapter.
The conversation screen

The buttons at the top manage the conversation.
- {rotate-ccw-clock} Opens a past conversation again, to resume it
- {square} Stops the conversation, which stays in the history
- {settings} Opens its settings
- {x} Closes the screen
Under the title, a line says what the AI is doing: thinking, reading, or waiting for your answer. If you leave the screen while it answers, the bubble carries a dot until you read its answer.
Start from scratch
Once the conversation is stopped with the square, touch the bubble and choose “Start a chat”. The AI starts from scratch. From one conversation to the next, it keeps only what the app holds.
Attach a tool\'s entries

Under the message, buttons add blocks.
- {type} A text
- {paperclip} A file, attached whole, or as a preview if it is long
- {camera} A photo
- {image} An image from the gallery
- {crosshair} A pointer
Each block is changed with the pencil and removed with the bin.

This time, add a pointer to a tool and tick Entries. Its entries then go with the message, over the period and with the filters chosen. Config would attach its settings. With nothing ticked, the AI only knows what you mean, and reads what it needs by itself.

Ask for instance “Sum up my entries of the week”, then send.
When the AI answers

The AI may ask you a question. Pick an answer, or else “Reply with a message”, or “Add a note” to your choice.

Before changing what you protect, it asks for your approval: “Allow” or “Refuse”. If the data it asks for goes past your threshold, the app asks you whether to send it.

While it works, touch “Interrupt” to stop its round. To copy a message, press and hold it.
Require your approval in this conversation

For a conversation where you want to check everything, touch the gear. Under “Also ask for my approval on”, tick for instance “The tools\' data”. Until the conversation ends, the AI will ask for your approval before each write to a tool. These boxes add to the protections already set.
Reasoning and costs

In the same settings, “Reasoning” sets how much the AI thinks before answering, for this conversation only. The more it thinks, the slower and dearer it is.\n\nThe statistics button, next to the gear, details what the conversation cost: what went out, what came back, and what was read again from the cache, cheaper because already sent.
Identities
An identity is a character the AI speaks as: Jung to read dreams, a drawing teacher for sketches. The work in the tools stays the same, only the answers change voice.
You can now talk to someone in particular. An identity is changed at any time on its screen, and a change counts from the next answer.
What an identity is

An identity has a voice, the way it speaks, a mind, the way it thinks, and a portrait, who it is. It may also have a bagage: resources it reads when it needs them, like a vocabulary or a list of references.\n\nWhen it speaks, its answers, its questions and the texts it writes in your tools are in its voice. The names of zones, tools and fields stay plain, so that they read well everywhere in the app.
Import an identity

In Settings › Identities, touch Import and choose an identity file. The app shows who it is and when it was published, then asks the Language it speaks, among those of the file.\n\nImporting the same identity again replaces it whole. The confirmation says what you would lose first, like the texts you changed by hand.
Read and change it

Touch an identity to open it. Its Voice, its Mind and its Portrait show laid out, with their size, and the Bagage lists its resources, each with a description that says when to call it up.\n\nEdit opens a text as it is written, to change it. New identity creates one from a name and a language, to write by hand. The AI can also read and change an identity, with your approval when it is protected.
Talk to it

Three ways to talk to an identity.
- In a zone's configuration, choose its Identity: the top of the zone then shows it, and its button opens a new conversation with it
- In a conversation, before the first message, the button at the right of the composer chooses who speaks
- A routine has its own Identity, its zone's at first
In the demo, the Italian zone speaks with Giulia, an Italian teacher written by hand, and so does its Sunday lesson routine.
Once the first message is sent, who speaks is fixed: open another conversation to talk to someone else.
Appearance
The User interface screen, in the Settings, sets how the whole app looks: its theme, its light or dark mode, its hue, its layout and its size.
The app now looks the way you want. Everything can be changed again in the same place, in Settings › User interface.
Choose a theme

In Settings › User interface, the Theme decides how the app is drawn: its shapes, its letters, its icons. Default is clear and sober, Cosy is round and bouncy, Retro is pixel art, Swiss is a poster in black, white and red, Ink and wash is painted with a brush on cream paper. Metro looks like metro signage, Cut paper like coloured sheets cut out on kraft paper, Blueprint like a plan drawn in fine lines on grid paper, E-reader like the screen of an e-reader, in pure black and white, where nothing moves.

A theme you choose applies at once, so you can see it. Save to keep it: if you leave the screen without saving, the app goes back to the theme it had.

With the Mode, the app turns Light, Dark, or As the phone, following its changes.
Adjust the display

Six more settings adjust the display.
- Hue: turns the theme's colours round the colour wheel, by degree. At 0, the theme keeps its own. The colours of states and tags stay as they are. E-reader, in black and white, has no hue.
- Interface size: makes the interface larger by steps, in the themes drawn pixel by pixel like Retro, which ignore Android's text size
- One column: the tiles one under the other, for a narrow screen. The arrows of the layout mode then move a tile up or down the column.
- Home screen title: the app's name and mark under the buttons of the home screen. Off, the zones come up.
- Interface sounds: the sounds the theme plays when you touch the screen. Only Cosy and Retro have some.
- Textures: how strongly the motifs chosen for zones and tools show, Subtle or Marked.
Your data
Your data stays on the phone. In Settings › Data management, you keep it safe, share a part of it, restore it, or start again from scratch. In Settings › History, you undo a change.
Your data is safe, and you know how to restore it or undo a change. Everything is set in Settings › Data management and Settings › History.
Turn on the automatic backup

In Settings › Data management, the Automatic backup keeps a copy of all the data in a folder of the phone. Touch “Choose the folder” and pick one.

A copy is written at most once an hour, only when the data changed. The app keeps four of them: the last hour, the last day, the last week and the last month. If a sync app follows that folder, the copies are also kept off the phone.

The Automatic backup switch stops it or starts it again, and “Change the folder” lets you pick another one.
Export, import or erase

The same screen is also where you export, import or erase everything.
- Export…: writes into the app's folder a part of the app, to share it, or everything, a full backup. Share then sends the file wherever you like.
- Import…: opens a file to take a part of it back, added to what you have. From a full backup, Restore everything replaces all the data, then restarts the app.
- Reset all the data: deletes everything, for good, then restarts the app.
The app asks for confirmation before restoring everything or resetting. A copy from the automatic backup is a full backup like any other.
Undo a change

In Settings › History, every change made by you, by the AI or by an outside AI is kept, the latest first.
- Undo: takes back the latest change
- Redo: puts back the last change undone
Touch a change to see what it modified, field by field, and to undo it alone. A change modified since can no longer be undone, and the screen says why.

Days of history and Room for the history (MB) say how long and how much the history keeps. The AI can also undo a change, when you ask it to. Restore everything and Reset all the data empty the history.
External access

With the external access, an AI running elsewhere, like Claude, ChatGPT, or an open model on your computer with LM Studio, reads and writes in the app like the built-in AI. The phone itself serves as the connector, in Settings › External access.
An outside AI can now work in the app, within the limits you give it. The access opens again from the same place whenever you need it.
What the external access does

An outside AI plugs into the app as a connector, once. From then on, it has the same commands as the built-in AI: reading the tools, writing in them, setting them up.\n\nThe access does not stay open: you open it when you want to use it, and it closes by itself after 30 minutes without a call. A write to what you protect waits for your approval, asked through a notification.
Choose the way in

The Way in says how the outside AI reaches the phone.
- Tailscale: the app publishes its own address, with a free Tailscale account
- Relay: through a relay you host. Then give, under Relay, the Relay address and the Relay secret.

The Data size per read is the most the outside AI receives at once. Beyond it, a read of several entries is refused and the AI asks for less; anything else comes in slices. It weighs on the outside AI's memory, not on your API key.
Open the access

With Tailscale, first touch “Connect the app to Tailscale”. Connecting creates the account if you have none. If the account is not ready yet, the screen says what to do, with a button for each case: “Turn on Funnel”, “Open the access policy” and “Copy the block”, or “Open the DNS page”. The access opens by itself once the account is set.\n\nTouch “Open the access”. The screen shows the address to give the outside AI. The first time, wait for the message “Address ready” before adding it in the client: publishing takes a few minutes. “Close the access” closes it at once, and “Disconnect from Tailscale” removes the app from the account.
Authorize an outside AI

In the outside AI, add a connector with this address. A page opens with a code, and the phone shows a notification. Type the code on the phone and touch Allow, or Refuse if the request is not yours.

The AI then shows in Authorized clients, with the date it was last used.
- Access: what it may touch. Empty, it can do everything, otherwise only what is listed.
- Revoke: takes its access away. To come back, it will have to be authorized again, with a new code.
When something goes wrong
When something does not work, the app helps you understand why and report it. Everything is in the Settings: Report a bug, and Error logs.
You know how to report a problem and read what the app noted. A report read over carefully helps get it fixed quickly.
Report a bug

In Settings › Report a bug, the app prepares a report: the versions of the app and the phone, the app's last stop if there was one, and the errors of the last two hours.

Describe what happened in the field “What happened”, if you like. The screen then shows exactly what will go. Ids and the content of your tools are masked.

“Send to the developer” prepares a mail with the report, in your mail app. “Share…” sends it through another app, to whoever you like. The copy button, at the top, copies the report: with no mail app on the phone, the screen gives the address to send it to.
When the app stopped

If the app stops suddenly, it says so at the next launch, with the screen “The app stopped”.
- See the report: opens the report, which holds this stop
- Continue: starts the app as usual
The report keeps this stop until the next one, so you can also send it later.
Read the logs

In Settings › Error logs, you read what the app noted while it ran, the most recent lines at the top.
- Minimum level: shows only the lines At least of that level, from Debug to Error
- Tag (empty = all): shows only one category of lines
- From: the period read, from a few minutes to Always
The app keeps only its most recent lines: read them soon after the problem.
Relative dates
A relative date is worked out from a moment, like “the day before” or “the current week”. It saves changing a period by hand every day.

## An example
A routine sums up the day every evening at 9 pm. Its message points to the Meals tool, over the period “The same day”. Every evening, the app reads that period again and sends the day's meals, without you changing anything.

## Choosing a relative date
When choosing a date, take Relative date, then:
- a Unit: hour, day, week, month or year
- an offset: the same day, the day before, 3 days before…
- a Moment: the Start or the End of that period
For example, “The day before”, from its Start to its End, covers the whole of yesterday.

The other choices are a Custom date, always fixed, Now, and No limit for a period open on one side.

## Relative to what
Under the choice, the screen shows the starting moment: “Relative to: …”.
- A routine starts from its scheduled time. If it runs late, the next morning, it still reads the meals of the planned day.
- A variable starts from the instant it is read. “Today's glasses” gives today's, and in a chart, those of each day shown.
- A chart starts from the moment it is shown: “the last 30 days” move on by a day every day.

## When the date stays fixed
In a conversation or in an entry, there is no starting moment. Choosing “Yesterday” simply gives yesterday's date, shown under the choice (“That is: 13 October”), and that date is what is kept. Read again in a month, it will still mean 13 October.

## Where a day starts
A day of the app does not have to start at midnight. In Settings › Format and dates, the Hour the day starts at and the Day the week starts on set the calendar of the whole app. With days starting at 4 am, it is still the day before at 0:30 am: a run noted at that time counts for the day before, in charts, variables and goals. “The current week” starts on the day chosen.
Protections

With protections, you choose what the AI must show you before changing it, and what a routine or an outside AI may touch. By default, only the values already noted are, against a configuration change that would remove them.

## An example
The Weight tool holds two years of measurements, and you don't want an AI to delete some by mistake. In its configuration, tick Data validation. From then on, before adding, changing or deleting an entry of Weight, the AI shows you what it wants to do and waits for “Allow” or “Refuse”.

## Three levels
Each level protects what it holds directly, and only that.
- The app: Protect the home screen, in Settings › AI validation. The AI asks before creating, changing or deleting a zone, or changing the home screen's groups.
- A zone: Protect this zone's content, in its configuration. The AI asks before touching its tools and their settings, its groups, its routines and its variables.
- A tool: Data validation, in its configuration. The AI asks before touching its entries.
Protecting a zone therefore does not protect its tools' entries. For that, also tick Data validation in each tool.

## Data already recorded
A configuration change can touch the entries already noted. Removing a field erases its values, narrowing a scale removes those past its bounds. Protect recorded data, in Settings › AI validation, is ticked from the start. Before such a change, the AI shows you how many values it removes or reads differently, and waits for your approval, whether the zone is protected or not.

## For a single conversation
You can also ask for more care for a single conversation, without changing your settings. In its settings, under “Also ask for my approval on”, tick for example “The tools' data”. Until the conversation ends, the AI then asks for your approval before writing in any tool, protected or not.

The two other boxes do the same for the home screen and its zones (“The home screen and the zones”), and for what each zone holds (“The zones' content”).

## Routines and outside AIs
A routine runs without you, so it cannot ask you anything. Instead, the Access of this routine says what it may touch. Empty, it can do everything. Otherwise, it touches only the zones and tools listed, each in read, use or full:
- read: reading
- use: writing entries, and in a zone, creating and changing its tools and variables
- full: also changing their own settings
A routine that writes a summary only needs to read: give it its tools in read.

An outside AI has the same kind of access, set in External access. Its writes to what you protect also wait for your approval, asked through a notification.

Only a person can change a protection, never the AI, a routine or an outside AI.
Field types
A field added to a tool notes one more piece of information in each entry. Its type decides what goes in it: a number, a choice, a duration…

## An example
In a Journal, you want to note your mood with each entry. In the tool's configuration, add a field, give it the Name of the field “Mood” and the Field type Choice. Then add three Options, Calm, Happy and Tired, each with its Color.

Each new journal entry then offers these three choices. Later, a chart can count the calm days, and the AI reads the mood as you do.

## The types
- Text: a few words or a page. The Text length sets its maximum size. Long or Unlimited, it takes formatting: the two buttons beside its name make a list or a numbered list, and a selected word turns Bold or Italic.
- Numeric: a number, like a weight. It takes a Unit, a Minimum, a Maximum and a Number of decimals.
- Scale: a rating between two bounds, with a Step. A Minimum label and a Maximum label say what the ends mean, like 1 “exhausted” and 10 “in shape”.
- Choice: one option from a list. With Multiple selection, several can be ticked. With Ranking, they are put in an order. With Open, a new value joins the options, like tags.
- Boolean: yes or no. A Label for true and a Label for false replace these words, like “Done” and “Not done”.
- Range: two numbers, a start and an end, like a price range.
- Date, Time, Date and time: a day, a time of day, or both. The time has its Time format.
- Duration: a length of time, like a commute. The Units are those entered and shown, from the largest to the smallest: hours minutes for time spent, days hours for a delay.
- Reference: a link to another thing in the app, like a meal's food. The Connect tools chapter shows it.
- Image: photos, taken with the camera or picked from the gallery. Most images limits them, 1 for a single photo. The AI can file a photo sent in a conversation there.

## For every field
- Description (optional): a hint, for you and for the AI, about what the field expects
- Always show (even when empty): otherwise, the field shows only once filled in
- Default value: filled in a new entry, which you can change before saving
- Read-only for the AI: the AI reads the field but never writes it, for what the AI cannot know, such as how something felt
Formulas and variables
A computed variable follows a formula, a calculation written with the names of its terms and of other variables. This chapter says what a formula can write, and what the app does with its value.

## An example
A Running tool notes the distance and the time of each run. A variable speed, of Kind Formula, has two terms: km, the sum of the week's distances, and time, the sum of the times. Its Formula is km / hours(time). It gives the week's average speed, and its Unit, km/h, is given by hand.

## What a formula writes
- the four operations, + - × ÷, or * and / on the keyboard
- parentheses, for the order of the calculation
- hours(), minutes() and seconds(), which turn a duration into a number: hours(time) is 1.5 for 1 h 30
- the names of the terms, and those of the app's other variables
A renamed variable stays in the formulas that read it, under its new name.

## A formula in each entry
A term “Reading of entries” can read “A formula in each entry”. The calculation is then done entry by entry, and the Reduction gathers them. In a Meals tool that names its food with a Reference field, quantity × food.kcal_100g / 100 gives the kcal of each meal, and the Sum those of the day. The dot reads a field of the thing named.

## The type of the value
The Type of the value is Deduced from the formula. A Sum keeps its field's unit, and the difference of two values in kcal stays in kcal. A number written in the formula takes the unit of what it meets: (eaten - burnt) / 7 stays in kcal. Anything else gives a number without a unit, like the speed of the example, whose Unit is completed by hand.

## When the value cannot be worked out
The variable then shows the reason in place of its value, never 0:
- a term that cannot be read, like an Average without any entry over its period. Without an entry, a Sum and a Count are 0.
- an entry without an answer to the field read. In the term, a filter “answered” on that field, added with Filters…, sets these entries aside.
- a division by zero
- a variable read that was deleted
A formula that writes an unknown name, or a variable that would end up reading itself, is not saved.

## When it is worked out
Nothing of its value is kept. It is worked out again at each reading, its periods counted from that moment: in a chart, for each day shown. The chapter “Relative dates” says more.
Conditions and filters
A condition compares two values, like “duration < 6 h”. It judges a goal, keeps part of the entries, or changes how a chart is drawn.

## An example
To talk to the AI about short nights, add a pointer to the Sleep tool, then touch “Filters and fields…”. Touch New filter, choose the Field duration, the Condition <, and write 6 h. Only the nights under 6 hours go with the message.

## Once, or on each entry
A condition is judged in two ways.
- Once, to say yes or no. In a Goal, each criterion has its Condition, like “Sleep, duration, average ≥ 7 h”. It compares two terms: a written value, a variable or a reading.
- On each entry, to keep only those where it is true. That is a filter: one is set in a pointer, and in a variable's term with Filters….
In a Chart, a colour can follow a Condition, row by row. Its When compares the columns of the row, like “kcal > 2000” to mark the days over.

## The operators
What can be compared depends on the field's type:
- a number, a duration, a date or a time: <, ≤, =, ≥, >, and between two values
- a date and time: the same, without =, two instants hardly ever falling on the same second
- a text: = and contains
- a choice: is one of, for one or several options
- every type: no answer, answered
A filter compares a field with a written value, like 6 h or an option.

## Both sides at the same moment
Both sides of a condition are read at the same moment. In a Goal, it is the end of the attempt, or now while it runs. To compare two periods, each is said in its term: “weight, average, the previous month” against “weight, average, the current month”.
Changing a tool\'s fields
The entries already noted follow their tool\'s fields. Before saving a changed field, the app says what the change removes from the entries.

## An example
In a Journal, the field Mood has three options: Calm, Happy and Tired. Remove Tired from its Options and save. The window “Confirmation of the changes” says how many values go: the entries that said Tired no longer have an answer. Nothing changes before you confirm.

## What is kept, and what goes
- A field removed, or a type changed, removes that field's values.
- An option removed removes the answers that chose it.
- A scale narrowed removes the values beyond it. Widened, it keeps its values, which read differently: a 4 out of 5 becomes a 4 out of 10.
- A choice turned to Multiple selection keeps each answer, in a list of one answer. The other way, a list of a single answer becomes an answer again, and the others go.
- A setting of the tool that makes a field required opens “Values needed”: the value the entries without one take.

## A new field instead
When the change touches a field's meaning (its type, a scale's bounds, the number of answers of a choice), the window offers “Create a new field”. The former one stays with all its values, renamed “Mood (before 21 October)”, and the new one starts empty.

## The other tools
A chart can filter on an option, like “moment is one of lunch”. Removing or renaming that option would leave this filter finding nothing. The window then names the tool that uses it, to correct it afterwards.

## What does not move
A closed attempt of a Goal keeps its own copy of its definition, and a finished Session keeps its steps. Changing their tool does not touch them.

## Going back
A confirmed change is undone in Settings › History, with the values it removed. When the AI changes a field, it shows the same counts and waits for your agreement: the chapter “Protections” explains how.
